A_target.statement:
Let $A$ be a [[Definition:Type|type]] and $B$ a type family over $A$.
The [[Definition:Dependent Product Type|dependent product type]] $\displaystyle \prod_{x : A} \map B x$ has as terms the functions $\lambda a. \map b a$ assigning to each $a : A$ a term $\map b a : \map B a$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\map P x$ be a [[Definition:Predicate|predicate]] on $A$.
A proof of $\forall x : A: \map P x$ is a method giving, for each $a : A$, a proof of $\map P a$.

validity_conditions: forall-introduction (assume arbitrary x, prove P(x)) corresponds to lambda-abstraction building a dependent function.
forall-elimination (instantiate at a) corresponds to function application at a.
So universal quantification transports to the Pi-type, generalizing the non-dependent function/implication case.
proof_plan: Read the [[Definition:Predicate|predicate]] $\map P x$ as a type family $\map B x$.
Map [[Definition:Universal Generalisation|$\forall$-introduction]] to $\lambda$-abstraction over $x$, producing a dependent function.

Map [[Definition:Universal Instantiation|$\forall$-elimination]] to application at a specific $a$:
:$f : \displaystyle \prod_{x : A} \map B x, \, a : A \vdash f \, a : \map B a$

Hence $\forall$ corresponds to the [[Definition:Dependent Product Type|dependent product type]].
{{qed}}
